
In this part of the practical, we will use what we have learned so far to perform the same analysis you have already learned with other tools, but this time using Python.

1. Download the datasets for this exercises and save them in your `data` folder:
  
  - [ParkRun Performance Data.xlsx](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/itsleeds/introds/refs/heads/main/00_data/ParkRunPerformanceData.xlsx)
  - [Running Data.xlsx](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/itsleeds/introds/refs/heads/main/00_data/RunningData.xlsx)
  
2. Download the following scripts and try to run the code in them. Your job is to **debug these scripts** by fixing the intentional errors so they run correctly.
  
  - Script 1: Excel Task ([Python](https://github.com/itsleeds/introds/blob/main/4-statistics/task_excel_debug.py), [R](https://github.com/itsleeds/introds/blob/main/4-statistics/task_excel_debug.R))
  - Script 2: SPSS Task ([Python](https://github.com/itsleeds/introds/blob/main/4-statistics/task_2_spss_debug.py), [R](https://github.com/itsleeds/introds/blob/main/4-statistics/task_2_spss_debug.R))

**R version:** If you prefer R, the same exercises are available in R. See the R script links above.

## More Debugging Practice

If you want more of the same once those two scripts run, the follow-on course [Python for Transport & Civil Engineering](https://github.com/chris-r-uol/python_learning) has a **traceback safari**: six short scripts, each containing one deliberate error, with a marker that reports which ones you have fixed without telling you how to fix them. It uses only the Python standard library, so there is nothing to install.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/chris-r-uol/python_learning.git
cd python_learning/week1_setup/exercises
python check.py
```

Python only — this exercise has no R version.
